::: {.why}
There is exactly one diffusion that reproduces every option price you can see today, which sounds like a complete answer and is not, and knowing why is the point of this week.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State what local volatility is and what the Dupire equation recovers from a surface.
- Say what local volatility predicts about how the smile moves when the spot moves, and whether that prediction is right.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Implement local volatility from your fitted SVI surface using the Dupire formula, and check that pricing with it reproduces the market prices you calibrated to. That reproduction is guaranteed by construction, so a failure means an implementation error rather than a model failure.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Test the dynamic prediction, which is where it fails: local volatility implies a specific movement of the smile as the spot moves, and that implied movement is empirically too strong. Compare consecutive days of your own surface data against what local volatility predicted, and report the discrepancy.
:::
:::
